domains.note: Cleanest transactional profile of any FK-heavy domain: patientId/appointmentId/treatmentCaseId are validated by a read before the transaction opens, never written cross-domain inside it. Already has a path-filtered CI workflow (windows-bridge-pr.yml).

No cross-domain prisma.$transaction touches billing models at all. earningService.ts/practitionerEarnings.ts/practitionerPayouts.ts/compensationRules.ts have zero dedicated tests - a gap to close in Stage 1/2, not a disqualifier.

Deceptively clean at import level. treatmentStockDeduction.ts writes InventoryItem/InventoryTransaction/Notification inside the SAME prisma.$transaction opened for TreatmentPlanProcedure completion (treatmentPlanProcedures.ts:151,271) - a real 3-domain (patients+inventory+notifications) write transaction. Zero test coverage. Not a good first-pilot despite low import fan-out.

Notification model has zero Prisma FKs to any other model, but is written to directly from inventory's cross-domain transaction. Zero dedicated test files; only incidental source-string assertions in unrelated suites.

labOrders/* subfolder is internally clean (zero external fan-out). Includes the one genuine transport-level route E2E test in the whole suite (externalCalendarWebhookRouteE2E.test.ts). Heavy real external-provider coupling (DigiDentiS, external calendar providers, Meta webhook transport).

Near-zero import-level fan-in (contrary to intuitive assumption) but is the FK target of most cross-domain writes and participant in 5 of 9 confirmed cross-domain transactions. MODULE_MAP: most-referenced model, 18+ relations. Regulatory/tenant-critical.

domains.boundaryClarityNote: 3 at import layer / 2 at schema layer - see note
domains.currentCouplingNote: 4 at import layer (zero fan-out) / 2 at schema layer (real R/W into Patient)
domains.note: Zero cross-domain file-import fan-out but real schema-level R/W into Patient (server/src/services/communicationConsent/legacyConsentCorrection.ts:302 mutates Patient.smsOptOut directly), corroborated by F0-004 PRV row (R/W/S into PAT, R/W into APT, R into TRC/DEN). 2nd-highest fan-out of F0-004's 37 domains (97 edges). Best-tested domain in the repo (~30 files, only domain with real-Postgres dbVerification coverage). Under active, in-flight KVKK regulatory remediation per RISK_REGISTER.md/CURRENT_PHASE.md (R-061 OPEN). This is the evidence basis for NOT selecting privacy as pilot despite it being the current blocker domain.

Highest import fan-out of the 10 domains (5 target domains). F0-004: 2nd-highest fan-in of any of the 37 pre-existing domains (APT, 116 edges). appointmentRequests.ts:305 conversion transaction spans patients+appointments+integrations, repeated across 5 near-identical call sites.

domains.importFanOutNote: 3 target domains but dozens of individual import lines (13+ into privacy, 13+ into AI)
domains.note: Highest change frequency by far (192 touches/120d, ~3x next domain). F0-004: highest fan-out of any of the 37 pre-existing domains (WHA, 106 edges) - 'god module' signature, consistent with routes/whatsapp.ts being 3999 lines with only ~380 being actual route handlers. Contains all 9 confirmed X (high-risk boundary violation) edges: direct Patient/Appointment writes from WhatsApp/Instagram AI flows bypassing the advisory-lock pattern used elsewhere.

domains.tenantRiskNote: N/A - no Prisma models of its own
domains.crossDomainTransactionSitesNote: 0 of its own; participates in messaging's 3 transaction sites since AI code physically executes inside those transactions
domains.note: Zero prisma.* calls in googleAiStudio.ts/whatsappConversationAgent.ts - no data-layer footprint. F0-004's PAI (AI Platform) row/column entirely empty, consistent with F0-003's 'confirmed absent, not merely unverified' finding. routes/whatsapp.ts imports 7 of 10 AI files; metaWhatsAppAiProcessor.ts and instagramAiConversationProcessor.ts (both inside messaging's own subfolders) import 6 AI files each; whatsappBookingFlow.ts:20 imports back into messaging - bidirectional, not one-way. Not extractable as a data-domain module today; only a stateless-service (prompt/NLU/schema files, already DB-free) extraction is realistic.

rationale: Zero cross-domain import coupling in both directions (0 fan-out, 0 fan-in among the 10 candidate domains)

Cleanest transactional profile of any FK-heavy domain - all 5 own prisma.$transaction sites are domain-internal, FK values validated by a pre-transaction read, never written cross-domain inside the transaction
Lowest business-criticality-weighted blast radius among low-coupling candidates (degrades an optional feature, not money movement or clinical continuity)
Lowest change frequency of the FK-heavy domains (30 touches/120d)
Already has a path-filtered CI workflow (windows-bridge-pr.yml) - organizational precedent for isolated CI treatment
primary.caveat: Reusable-pattern value scored lower (3/5) than billing's (5/5) because of idiosyncratic hardware/Windows-bridge/DICOM content that won't generalize to the next module; the reusable part is the process (Stage 1-7), not the domain content.

rationale: Equal-lowest import coupling (0 fan-out, 1 read-only fan-in edge)
Zero cross-domain prisma.$transaction sites at all - only dependency is a safely-splittable two-phase read-then-write
Zero external provider coupling - cleanest 'pure backend module' pattern instance, highest reusable-pattern value (5/5)
One small tenant-scoping gap (PaymentPlanInstallment.clinicId), additive fix
fallback.whenToPreferOverPrimary: If reviewers judge imaging's hardware-bridge idiosyncrasies make it a poor template for subsequent pure-TypeScript modules

explicitlyUnsuitableAsFirstPilot.reason: Highest import fan-out of the 10 domains (5 target domains); F0-004 confirms 2nd-highest fan-in of the 37 pre-existing domains (116 edges); central participant in the richest cross-domain transaction in the repository (patients+appointments+integrations, 5 near-identical call sites).

F0-004 confirms highest fan-out of the 37 pre-existing domains (WHA, 106 edges); contains all 9 confirmed high-risk boundary-violation writes into Patient/Appointment; by far the highest change frequency in the repository (192 touches/120d, ~3x next domain) - too much concurrent churn to safely re-draw a boundary around right now.

Most cross-domain-referenced Prisma model (18+ relations per MODULE_MAP); direct participant in 5 of 9 confirmed cross-domain transactions; regulatory/tenant-critical clinical core entity; coupling is schema-level, not visible to a naive import-count check.

Task explicitly warns against defaulting to this domain because it is the current blocker; evidence independently supports the warning: real schema-level R/W into Patient (not fully decoupled despite zero import-level fan-out); 2nd-highest fan-out of F0-004's 37 domains (97 edges) and very high fan-in from messaging; KVKK/regulatory risk (a defect here is a compliance incident, not just a bug); already under active, in-flight regulatory remediation (RISK_REGISTER.md R-061 OPEN); DEPENDENCY_MAP's own F0-007 addendum states its PRV/WHA/SMS/REC cells are already known to be provisional pending further in-flight KVKK-HIGH-007 work.

No Prisma models, zero prisma.* calls, no data-layer footprint to extract (F0-004's PAI row/column entirely empty); bidirectionally entangled with messaging with no existing interface boundary; modularizing it first would really be a disguised, premature attempt to modularize messaging.

recommendation.minimalFirstRationale: No prior working ESLint setup required; pure Node with no Windows-compatibility risk; rule model maps directly onto DEPENDENCY_MAP.md's existing P/R/W/S/X vocabulary; ship scoped to the pilot domain only at first with an allowlist/baseline for all other domains' pre-existing edges (notably messaging's 9 known X violations) so Stage 7 does not silently require fixing unrelated domains.
recommendation.futureOptionRationale: More expressive long-term choice (public.ts/private-module contract modeling, ecosystem-standard, editor-integrated real-time feedback) but requires first fixing the repository's currently non-functional ESLint setup - a separate, currently-unbudgeted piece of work not recommended to bundle into the first pilot's Stage 7.

impactOnThisTasksFindings.imagingCandidateScore: Unchanged numerically. Refinement only: F2-PREP-001 splits 'imaging' into two 38-domain-taxonomy entries - IMG (Imaging - Server Ingest and Viewer) and BRG (Imaging - Device Bridge / Windows Bridge). This task's own 'imaging' bucket already spanned both (it cites the ImagingBridgePairingDevice tenant-scoping gap, a BRG-owned model). F2-PREP-001's domain-summary table flags 'Ownership ambiguity: YES' for both IMG and BRG, but its own per-domain JSON detail clarifies this is not a true ownership dispute: IMG = 'none significant on the ownership question itself'; BRG = 'bridge-agent/ and windows-bridge/ internal structure is unverified by this task' (those are separate deployables outside the CODEGRAPH-DISCIPLINE-scoped root set both tasks used - a shared, pre-existing scope limit, not a new gap). Net effect: no change to the primary-candidate recommendation; F2-PREP-005 should treat the Device Bridge's external deployable internals as an explicit due-diligence item before any Stage 1 work on that sub-scope.
impactOnThisTasksFindings.billingFallbackScore: Unchanged. F2-PREP-001 independently confirms this task's 'billing' bucket (routes/payments.ts, paymentPlans.ts, insuranceProvisions.ts, compensationRules.ts, practitionerEarnings.ts, practitionerPayouts.ts, financeDashboard.ts, services/earningService.ts) is a distinct concept from the separately-tracked, unimplemented 'PBL - Billing / Subscription Engine' domain (0 Prisma models, 0 routes, 0 services, classification 'planned/not implemented' per F2-PREP-001). No score change; this reconciliation makes the distinction explicit to prevent future readers conflating the two.
impactOnThisTasksFindings.integrationsScore: Potentially understated, not changed by this task. This task's independent 'integrations' bucket (scored 3s across most criteria, see domainScoring) was assembled from pieces of the old 37-domain taxonomy with no single clean analogue (per this task's own methodological note). F2-PREP-001 now names a formal 38th domain, External Calendar Integration (EXC), with its own dedicated routes/services/jobs/provider-factory pattern that did not exist at this task's independent-research scope and is not the same thing this task scored as 'integrations'. F2-PREP-001 itself observes EXC 'already exhibits essentially the full target module shape' (explicitly flagged there as an observation, not a selection). This task does not retroactively score EXC across all 14 criteria - that would require the same depth of independent transaction/coupling/test analysis given to the other 10 domains, which is out of scope for a reconciliation pass. EXC is instead added to the set F2-PREP-005 must compare (see pilotSelection.mustBeComparedByF2Prep005).
impactOnThisTasksFindings.migrationWaveOrder: Unchanged by this task. Flagged for F2-PREP-005: EXC's clean-slate shape (no legacy code to migrate, already provider-port-shaped) may make it a stronger M1/M2 candidate than this task's original wave plan anticipated, but EXC's cross-domain dependency edges are not yet coded into the accepted DEPENDENCY_MAP.md matrix (per F2-PREP-001 itself), so this task does not unilaterally reorder waves to include it.
impactOnThisTasksFindings.pilotRiskAssumptions: Reinforced, not changed. F2-PREP-001's ContactRequest OWNERSHIP_AMBIGUOUS finding (Appointments vs. a channel-agnostic intake domain, unresolved) reinforces (does not newly introduce) this task's existing exclusion of Appointments as a first-pilot candidate. F2-PREP-001's Privacy ownership deltas (+4 Prisma models, +10 services since the F0-003/F0-004 baseline, all under the Privacy/Consent/Retention/DSR domain) reinforce this task's existing exclusion of privacy as a first-pilot candidate (an actively-growing domain is not a safer pilot than this task already concluded).
